To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
repeated Ag exposures exacerbate murine allergic airways diseases with prominent eosinophilia through a collaborative interaction between type 2 ILC2s and Ag-specific CD4 Th2 cells.
repeated Ag exposures exacerbate murine allergic airways diseases by enhancing the interactions between acquired Ag-specific CD4 Th2 cells and the innate ILC2 cells.
repeated Ag rechallenge exacerbates murine allergic airways diseases by promoting the interactions between CD4+ Th cells and ILC2s.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the collaborative interactions between ILC2s and CD4+ Th cells, which exacerbate allergic airway diseases in mice.
the role of innate and acquired lymphoid cells in the exacerbation of murine allergic airways diseases.
the collaborative interactions between innate and adaptive lymphocytes, and their roles in Ag-mediated exacerbation of allergic airway diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ILC2 cells and CD4+ Th cells are both necessary for the pathogenesis of allergic airway inflammation and that they are also both necessary for allergic airway diseases to become chronic.
